newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollars end down with S&P, await PPI.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollars end down with S&P, await PPI.

text.p: SIMEX Eurodollar futures ended lower on Wednesday after being sold off in late afternoon trade on the back of declines in the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond and in key December GLOBEX S&P 500 stock futures traded in Tokyo.

There was little consensus among dealers about the reason for the decline, but many attributed it to a newspaper report questioning whether Japanese institutions would continue to buy U.S. Treasury debt securities.

A Wall Street Journal report quoted a senior Goldman Sachs official as saying Japanese institutions were likely to slow their purchases of U.S. government securities, which could begin to push up interest rates.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.32 after falling to a low of 94.28 against their IMM close at 94.37. Turnover was a moderate 17,565 lots. March was at 94.45 against 94.48.
Dealers said the move, which also triggered falls in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, was exaggerated by thin market conditions.

"Now we've pushed the market into lower levels, people will look to the PPI (Producer Price Index) and CPI (Consumer Price Index) for a confirmation of the downtrend," said a trader with a European futures house, referring to U.S. inflation data due later on Wednesday and Thursday.
"But I don't think the data are going to provide any impetus to push the market lower. There's clearly no pressure in the pipeline pushing the U.S. into an inflationary spiral," he said.
March JGBs settled at 125.04 against their previous 125.67 after hitting a low of 124.95. September Euroyen was quoted one tick above its day low of 99.14 at 1125 GMT against its IMM close at 99.18.

Dealers said the market was unmoved by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita's comments to the Japanese Diet as he merely reiterated the view that Japan's economic recovery was not yet self-sustaining -- reaffirming the need for continued low interest rates.
